I compared the two supervision regimes' budgets concretely and recorded three claims: the closest work asserts a fair comparison with all hyperparameters, LoRA setup, sequence length, epochs and schedule held fixed and "the only difference... is the type of QA supervision" (C018); but maximum sequence length is a truncation cap rather than a fixed token count, so the CG arm still consumes more supervision tokens per target triple (C019); and the SFT stage is only LoRA on a single A100 80GB, far cheaper than the 4×H200 RL stage (C020).

I updated U002 to sharpened/partially resolved — the mechanism difference remains implementation-level, but no retrieved work (dynamic-triple VQA, subgraph-size study, SLiNT, CDTP) provides a token-matched or example-matched supervision-regime comparison, so attribution stays unestablished and is still targeted by experiment E001 — and recorded new uncertainty U019: whether the two arms even use the identical QA items/questions, a second possible confound beyond volume.
